transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I keep getting a swimmy, light-headed feeling when I stand up from a chair or get out of bed. It started about ten days ago, and I’m worried it might be the new blood-pressure tablet.
Have you ever had an allergic reaction or a bad reaction to any medicine?
I don’t have any allergies to medicines that I know of. The only thing I’m wondering about is whether this new blood-pressure tablet is causing the dizziness.
How much does that swimmy, light-headed feeling get in the way of your usual day?
I’d rate it about 6 out of 10. I nearly fell once and had to grab the kitchen worktop, and I’ve stopped going to my Tuesday lunch club because I’m worried about feeling faint on the bus.
Besides your blood pressure, has a doctor ever told you that you have any other ongoing health conditions?
Yes, I’ve got osteoarthritis in both hips. I’ve had high blood pressure for about 15 years.
When that swimmy, light-headed feeling comes on, does anything else happen at the same time?
No, I haven’t had chest pain, palpitations, blackouts, or weakness in my arms or legs. It just feels like I’m about to faint, not like the room is spinning.
Where do you notice that swimmy, light-headed feeling, and does it spread anywhere else?
It’s just a general swimmy, about-to-faint feeling, mostly when I stand up. I haven’t noticed it spreading anywhere else.
How often do you get that swimmy, light-headed feeling when you stand up?
It happens several times a day, and each episode lasts less than a minute. It’s worse first thing in the morning or if I stand up quickly, and it settles if I sit back down for a minute.
Other than what you've already told me, is there anything else about your past health that you think I should know?
No, I don’t think there’s anything else. Just the high blood pressure and the osteoarthritis in both hips.
Besides what you've already told me, is there anything else you’ve noticed when that swimmy feeling comes on?
No, I haven’t noticed anything else when it comes on.
Can you tell me about any medicines you take these days, including any new or recently changed ones and the dose if you know it?

I take amlodipine 5 mg once a day, which the practice nurse started about two and a half weeks ago; bendroflumethiazide 2.5 mg every morning, which I’ve taken for years; a small stomach tablet each morning that I can’t remember the name of; and paracetamol 1 g up to three times a day for my hip pain.
Is there anything else you'd like to add about the medicines you take?
No, that’s all the medicines I take. I’m mainly worried the new amlodipine is causing the dizziness, and I’d like to know whether I should stop it.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
